Formulation
Current presentation is dominated by dermatological symptoms (itchy, sore, cracked skin) impacting sleep, concentration, and daily functioning. No mental health disorder is identified or explicitly discussed. The patient shows insight and initiative in seeking help but expresses social discomfort discussing the condition with others.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Obtain rapid relief from distressing skin symptoms; improve sleep and daily functioning; resume normal activities (work, hiking)
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce itch and skin inflammation, support sleep restoration, address secondary functional impacts
- Actions (Patient): Use prescribed steroid cream, emollient, and antihistamine as directed; maintain symptom/trigger diary; monitor for improvement over 7–10 days; follow-up if no improvement
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe stronger steroid cream, fexofenadine, and emollient; provide guidance on trigger avoidance; recommend follow-up in 1 week if no improvement

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Not recorded

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Use of prescribed dermatological agents, importance of identifying triggers, use of over-the-counter vs. prescription treatments, when to seek review if not resolving
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistence or worsening of symptoms after 7–10 days, impaired sleep or daily functioning, increasing area/severity of rash
- Coping Strategies: Symptom diary; environmental/trigger modification; adherence to medication regimen
